scores.justification: Rigor of method / argument: The algebra is sound (code, distance k+1, Prop. 1 b-d, ramp arithmetic and the Lean field/RS code all check out), but the central statement about cards is false for the cards actually printed: Prop. 1(a) and Fig. 1 say a card satisfies the syndrome equations, then §4.2 says ("The printed parity words are computed over the data words and this header" — §4.2), so a printed card is a codeword only of the length-W+1 code. The digest definition in §4.3 does not match `Grid.digestWords`, the 2^-11d false-accept figure ignores the t-subset search, and the decoder's safety rests on a heuristic with no stated miscorrection bound.

Evidence sufficiency: Every table cell matches the harness logs, but several claims outrun them: the safety headline ("returned no wrong secret" — §5.3) is given with no upper bound (zero in 28,000 bounds the rate only near 1e-4, and at 0.75% per 400-trial cell); the foreign-card comparison withholds the digest from both baselines although the logs show joint decoding without the digest does no better; the 97.6% figure in §3.2 has no artifact; grids are never tested with swapped words, the motivating human error; and the header and dropped-word rows that were run are not reported.

Clarity of contribution: The paper opens on its organizing idea ("That is the claim of this paper." — §1) and separates inherited ingredients from the new arrangement, so each contribution is extractable in a sentence. One point off because the abstract's single quantitative comparison is the most favourable cell of Table 2 and the third contribution (header and digest) has no section pointer and no reported measurement.

Related-work positioning: The closest formats are cited, but SLIP39 is described only as ("protects each share with a three-word RS1024 checksum that its specification uses for detection" — §2); its share-set identifier and its digest of the shared secret, which address exactly the foreign-card failure the paper charges to per-share schemes, are not mentioned. Robust secret sharing, information dispersal and SSKR are absent; no litsearch sibling exists, so the score rests on the prose alone.

Reproducibility: Commands, toolchain and RNG seed are given and the logs are stored, but the paper points only to ("All numbers come from the accompanying source tree" — §8) with no URL, commit or archive; the one hash recorded with the logs predates the grid code, which is uncommitted. The digest and rescue step are under-specified relative to the code, and no test vectors are given, so an independent implementation would not interoperate.

Figure & table quality: Captions are self-contained, but Fig. 1 overprints its own labels in the PDF (the column arrow and "each column: Shamir" box cover "share words"; "k parity words" runs into "header"), Fig. 2 prints two pages after its discussion and its caption's ("Joint decoding gains little over per-card repair with one spare card" — Fig. 2 caption) sits beside a 20-point gap at 10%. Table 1 hides the ambiguous and unfiltered outcomes its text discusses, Table 4 mixes "0" and "refused", and no table or plot carries an uncertainty.

Prose & structural quality: Sentence-level prose is clean and free of AI tells, and the build log has no overfull boxes or unresolved references. Capped at 2 by the reader-flow rule: more than three confirmed define-before-use defects remain in the body, among them ("the original is the unique valid phrase within reach whenever" — §3.1), "dealing", "seed", the 30-word card used before §4.3, the unexplained 32 in the header, and "bursts" before "burn"; symbols n, N, d and h each change meaning between Sections 3 and 4.

Citation hygiene: All `\cite` keys resolve. Deductions: an empirical claim with no source ("Our cards use dictionary words, which resist transcription slips better than character strings" — §2); RAID-6 P/Q attributed to a paper that defines levels 1-5; and `refs.bib` carries wrong years (Blakley-Meadows and Krawczyk as 2007), proceedings typed as `@article` with "Lecture Notes in Computer Science" as journal, and one uncited entry.

Rhetorical economy: Ten pages with the claim in the first sentence and little padding. One point off for full restatements: the no-wrong-secret claim appears five times and the spare-card rule four ("Plan for one more card than the threshold to be present at recovery." — §6), and §8 repeats setup material from §5.1.

findings.rationale: R1: Prop. 1(a), Fig. 1 caption and the introduction say a card satisfies Eq. (1); the printed card includes the header contribution (Grid.applyHeader) and is a codeword only as a W+1-symbol word.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the card with its header before Prop. 1, restate (a) for the extended word, and give the row distance with the number known (k+1) and unknown (k).

findings.rationale: R2: Baselines are run without the digest; the logs' no-digest grid column shows joint decoding alone returns wrong secrets or refuses in the foreign-card rows, so the result belongs to the digest.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the no-digest grid column, add a card-parity-plus-digest baseline, and reword 5.3 and the conclusion.

findings.rationale: R3: SLIP39's share-set identifier and digest of the shared secret, and codex32's identifier, are not described although they address the foreign-card case charged to per-share schemes.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe these mechanisms in Related Work and present the foreign-card rows as 'linear checks alone'.

findings.rationale: R4: Zero wrong secrets in 28,000 trials is reported with no upper bound (about 1.1e-4 pooled, 0.75% per 400-trial cell), no breakdown, and no mention that card parity returned a wrong secret in the illegible-number row.
findings.suggested_fix: State the bound, the breakdown of 28,000 and the scope of the fault mix.

findings.rationale: R5: 'first d 11-bit groups of SHA-256' differs from Grid.digestWords, which takes the low 11 bits of successive big-endian 16-bit groups.
findings.suggested_fix: Align text and code and add a test vector.

findings.rationale: R6: The 97.6% development figure has no log, trial count or harness switch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the ablation to the harness and logs, or replace with a labelled estimate, or delete.

findings.rationale: R7: No grid scenario swaps words within a card, although swaps are the motivating human error and cards cannot use the BIP39 checksum filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a swap scenario to gridtests or state that it is untested.

findings.rationale: R8: Illegible-number, dropped-word and garbage rows exist in grid-main-k4.final but are not reported; the header contribution has no reported measurement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the three rows to Table 2.

findings.rationale: R9: No URL, commit or archive for the source; the recorded hash predates Grid.lean and GridTests.lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a public URL and the exact commit that produced the logs.

findings.rationale: R10: The cited study measures recall from memory; the sentence sits in a transcription argument and does not say so, and the 14 of 41 are budget-limited recoverable attempts.
findings.suggested_fix: Say what was measured and limit the inference to the shape of word errors.

findings.rationale: R11: The abstract's only comparison is the most favourable cell (3-of-5, all cards, 10%).
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause on 2-of-3 or the exactly-t case and say 10% is assumed.

findings.rationale: R12: 2^-11d is per candidate; the t-subset fallback multiplies it by C(m,t), and step 5 error-corrects the interpolated row rather than only verifying it.
findings.suggested_fix: State the union bound and describe step 5 as implemented.

findings.rationale: R13: n, N, d and h change meaning between Sections 3 and 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Use W for phrase length, keep N for mnemonic length, index rows by j.

findings.rationale: R14: Eight define-before-use defects in the body (within reach, seed, dealing, 30-word card, bursts, the constant 32, unfiltered numbers and 'ambiguous', '0' vs 'refused').
findings.suggested_fix: Define each at or before first use; see comments.md.

findings.rationale: R15: In the compiled PDF the column arrow and its label overprint 'share words' and two top labels collide.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the column annotation outside the grid and separate the top labels.

findings.rationale: R16: Robust secret sharing, information dispersal and SSKR are not cited; the words-vs-characters claim is unsourced; RAID-6 is attributed to a paper defining levels 1-5.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run paper-litsearch for these and fix the two citations.

findings.rationale: 'bursts far beyond it' compares an error bound with erasures.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare erasures with the erasure guarantee.

findings.rationale: 'unsafe' is not shown by the 24-word arithmetic (124 bits remain).
findings.suggested_fix: Argue from the missing threshold and the 12-word case.

findings.rationale: Half-width given for 400 trials only; other tables use 200, 250, 300.
findings.suggested_fix: Give 6.9, 6.2 and 5.7 points respectively.

findings.rationale: Same configuration quoted as 79% (5.4) and 83% (6) from separate runs with no bridge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one bridging sentence.

findings.rationale: '13--15%' is 13.0 and 15.5 in the log; percentages are truncated by the harness.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 13-16% and note truncation or round.

findings.rationale: Table 1 omits parity-only and ambiguous outcomes that the text relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the columns.

findings.rationale: Fig. 2 prints two pages after its discussion; no uncertainty shown; 'gains little' unquantified.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix placement, add intervals, quantify.

findings.rationale: Rescue-step conditions (>= 3 guessed positions, k >= 3, <= 14 open columns) are not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: State them.

findings.rationale: Wrong years for Blakley-Meadows and Krawczyk; proceedings typed as @article; one uncited entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the entries.

findings.rationale: No-wrong-secret claim stated five times; spare-card rule four times.
findings.suggested_fix: State each once in the body plus abstract and conclusion.

findings.rationale: Comment names the empty run grid-main-k4.txt.
findings.suggested_fix: Point to grid-main-k4.final.
